nodes.name: b-quad-graph
nodes.statement: A b-quad-graph $\mathscr{D}$ is a strongly regular cell decomposition of a domain in $\C$ with all 2-cells being quadrilaterals and 1-skeleton bipartite (vertices colored white/black).

nodes.name: Admissible labelling
nodes.statement: A labelling $\alpha:F(\mathscr{D})\to(0,\pi)$ is admissible if $\sum_{f \text{ incident to } v}\alpha(f)=2\pi$ at all interior black vertices $v\in V_{int}(G^*)$.

nodes.name: Admissibility condition
nodes.statement: $\sum_{f \text{ incident to } v} \alpha(f) = 2\pi$ at every interior black vertex $v\in V_{int}(G^*)$.

nodes.name: Immersed planar circle pattern
nodes.statement: A circle pattern for $(\mathscr{D},\alpha)$ is an indexed collection of circles $\{C_z\}$ and oriented kites $\{K_e\}$ satisfying intersection-angle, kite-sharing, and disk-cover conditions. Embedded if all kites have disjoint interiors; isoradial if all radii equal.

nodes.name: Radius function characterization
nodes.statement: For a planar circle pattern, the radius function $r$ satisfies $\bigl(\sum_{[z,z_0]\in E(G)} f_{\alpha([z,z_0])}(\log r(z)-\log r(z_0))\bigr)-\pi=0$ at every interior vertex; conversely such $r$ on simply connected $\mathscr{D}$ yields a unique pattern up to isometries of $\C$.
conclusions: Closing condition $\bigl(\sum_{[z,z_0]\in E(G)} f_{\alpha([z,z_0])}(\log r(z)-\log r(z_0))\bigr)=\pi$ holds at every interior vertex
Conversely, any such $r$ yields a planar circle pattern, unique up to isometries of $\C$

nodes.name: Closing condition for radii
nodes.statement: $\sum_{[z,z_0]\in E(G)} f_{\alpha([z,z_0])}(\log r(z)-\log r(z_0)) = \pi$, where $f_\theta(x)=\frac{1}{2i}\log\frac{1-e^{x-i\theta}}{1-e^{x+i\theta}}$, $0<f_\theta(x)<\pi$.

nodes.name: Properties of $f_\theta$
nodes.statement: (i) $f_\theta'(x)=\frac{\sin\theta}{2(\cosh x-\cos\theta)}>0$. (ii) $f_\theta(x)+f_\theta(-x)=\pi-\theta$.
conclusions: $f_\theta'(x)=\frac{\sin\theta}{2(\cosh x-\cos\theta)}>0$
$f_\theta(x)+f_\theta(-x)=\pi-\theta$

nodes.name: Inverse radius function
nodes.statement: If an isoradial circle pattern exists for $(G,\alpha)$ and $r$ is the radius function of any planar pattern, then $1/r$ is the radius function of another circle pattern for $(G,\alpha)$.
assumptions: An isoradial circle pattern for $(G,\alpha)$ exists
$r$ is the radius function of a planar circle pattern for $(\mathscr{D},\alpha)$
conclusions: There exists a circle pattern $\mathscr{C}$ for $(G,\alpha)$ with $r_{\mathscr{C}}=1/r$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma (Inverse radius function)
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lemPropf}(ii) the function $1/r$ satisfies condition $\eqref{eqFgen}$ at all interior vertices, using $\sum_{[z,z_0]\in E(G)}(\pi-\alpha([z,z_0]))=2\pi$ from existence of an isoradial pattern.

nodes.name: Hirota equation
nodes.statement: $w(x_0)w(y_0)a_0 - w(x_1)w(y_0)a_1 - w(x_1)w(y_1)a_0 + w(x_0)w(y_1)a_1 = 0$ for the comparison function $w$ on each face.

nodes.name: Comparison function
nodes.statement: For two circle patterns $\mathscr{C}_1,\mathscr{C}_2$ on $\mathscr{D}$, $w:V(\mathscr{D})\to\C$ is defined by $w(y)=r_2(y)/r_1(y)$ on $V(G)$ and $w(x)=e^{i\delta(x)}\in\Sp^1$ on $V(G^*)$ (rotation of edge-star).

nodes.name: Regular labelling $\alpha_\psi$ on $SG$
nodes.statement: For $\psi\in(0,\pi)$ and edge $[z_1,z_2]\in E(SG)$ with $\Re(z_1)<\Re(z_2)$: $\alpha_\psi([z_1,z_2])=\psi$ if $\Im(z_1)<\Im(z_2)$, else $\pi-\psi$.

nodes.name: Rigidity of $SG$-circle patterns
nodes.statement: Any embedded planar circle pattern $\mathscr{C}$ for $SG$ and $\alpha_\psi$ is the image of a regular isoradial circle pattern for $SG$ and $\alpha_\psi$ under a similarity.
assumptions: $\mathscr{C}$ is an embedded planar circle pattern for $SG$ and $\alpha_\psi$
conclusions: $\mathscr{C}$ is the image of a regular isoradial $SG$-circle pattern under a similarity of $\C$

nodes.name: Generalized Ring Lemma for $SG(3,0)$
nodes.statement: For an embedded circle pattern for $SG(3,0)$ and $\alpha_\psi$, there is $C=C(\psi)>0$ with $r(i^k(1+i))/r(0)>C$ for $k=0,1,2,3$.
assumptions: $r$ radius function of an embedded circle pattern for $SG(3,0)$ and $\alpha_\psi$
conclusions: There exists $C=C(\psi)>0$ independent of $r$ such that $r(i^k(1+i))/r(0)>C$ for $k=0,1,2,3$

nodes.name: Proof of Generalized Ring Lemma
nodes.statement: Assume the contrary: a sequence of patterns with $r_n(0)=1$ and $r_n(i^k(1+i))\to 0$. Pass to a subsequence converging in $\hat{\C}$; then $\eqref{eqFgen}$ forces some kites to overlap in the limit, contradicting embeddedness.

nodes.name: Bound on incident-radius ratio (corSn)
nodes.statement: There is an absolute $C>0$ such that for any embedded $SG$-circle pattern with $SG(n,v)\subset G$ for $n\geq 3$, all incident vertices $w$ to $v$ satisfy $1-\frac{C}{n}\leq \frac{r(w)}{r(v)} \leq 1+\frac{C}{n}$.
conclusions: $1-\frac{C}{n}\leq \frac{r(w)}{r(v)} \leq 1+\frac{C}{n}$ for all $w$ incident to $v$

nodes.name: Discrete conformal map
nodes.statement: A map $f:D\subset\Z^2\to\C$ is discrete conformal if all elementary quadrilaterals have cross-ratio $-1$: $q(f_{n,m},f_{n+1,m},f_{n+1,m+1},f_{n,m+1})=-1$. Embedded if interiors of distinct quadrilaterals are disjoint.

nodes.name: Discrete map $Z^\gamma$ (orthogonal)
nodes.statement: For $0<\gamma<2$, $Z^\gamma:\Z_+^2\to\C$ is the solution of $\eqref{defZgamma1}$ and $\eqref{defZgamma2}$ with $Z^\gamma(0,0)=0$, $Z^\gamma(1,0)=1$, $Z^\gamma(0,1)=e^{\gamma\pi i/2}$.

nodes.name: Properties of orthogonal $Z^\gamma$
nodes.statement: (i) $(\gamma-1)(R(z)^2-R(z-i)R(z+1))\geq 0$ for $z\in\V\setminus\{\pm N+iN\}$. (ii) For $0<\gamma<2$, $Z^\gamma$ is embedded; corresponding circle patterns are embedded.
conclusions: $(\gamma-1)(R(z)^2-R(z-i)R(z+1))\geq 0$ for all $z\in\V\setminus\{\pm N+iN\mid N\in\N\}$
$Z^\gamma$ is embedded; the corresponding circle pattern is embedded

nodes.name: Rigidity of orthogonal $Z^\gamma$-circle patterns
nodes.statement: For $\gamma\in(0,2)$ the infinite orthogonal embedded $Z^\gamma$-circle pattern is the unique embedded orthogonal circle pattern (up to global scaling) covering the sector of angle $\gamma\pi/2$ with boundary circle centers on the boundary half-lines.
assumptions: Embedded orthogonal circle pattern with kites covering $\{\rho e^{i\beta}:\rho\geq 0,\beta\in[0,\gamma\pi/2]\}$
Boundary circle centers lie on $\R_+$ and $e^{i\gamma\pi/2}\R_+$
conclusions: The pattern equals the $Z^\gamma$-circle pattern up to global scaling

nodes.name: Recurrence on $\Z^2$ networks
nodes.statement: (i) The simple random walk on $\Z^2$ is recurrent. (ii) If $c_2(e)\leq c_1(e)$ on all edges and $(\Z^2,c_1)$ is recurrent, then $(\Z^2,c_2)$ is recurrent.
conclusions: Simple random walk on $\Z^2$ is recurrent
If $c_2\leq c_1$ on all edges and $(\Z^2,c_1)$ recurrent, then $(\Z^2,c_2)$ recurrent

nodes.name: Subharmonicity of radius ratio (orthogonal)
nodes.statement: For two orthogonal circle patterns on $SG(1,0)$ with radii $\rho_j,r_j$: $\sum_{j=1}^4 c_j r_j/\rho_j \geq \sum c_j r_0/\rho_0$ and similarly for $\rho/r$, with $c_j=1/((\rho_j/\rho_0)+(\rho_0/\rho_j))$.
assumptions: Two orthogonal circle patterns for $SG(1,0)$ with radii $\rho_j$ and $r_j$
conclusions: $\sum_{j=1}^4 c_j (r_j/\rho_j) \geq \sum_{j=1}^4 c_j (r_0/\rho_0)$
$\sum_{j=1}^4 c_j (\rho_j/r_j) \geq \sum_{j=1}^4 c_j (\rho_0/r_0)$

nodes.name: Recurrence iff superharmonic functions constant
nodes.statement: A network is recurrent if and only if every nonnegative superharmonic function on it is constant.
assumptions: Network on a graph with positive conductances
conclusions: Network is recurrent iff every nonnegative superharmonic function is constant

nodes.name: Proof of rigidity of orthogonal $Z^\gamma$-circle patterns
nodes.statement: Compare the two radius functions $R$ and $r$ via $f_1=r/R$, $f_2=R/r$; show both are subharmonic with respect to recurrent conductance networks, hence constant by Theorem~\ref{theosuperharm}, so $r\equiv R$.

nodes.name: Set up two networks $(\Z^2,C),(\Z^2,\tilde{C})$
nodes.statement: Use Lemma~\ref{corSn} and the Ring Lemma to bound $r(z_j)/r(z_0)$ by $K$; define conductances $C(e)=(R_j/R_k+R_k/R_j)^{-1}$ and $\tilde C$ similarly.

nodes.name: Both networks are recurrent
nodes.statement: Since $C,\tilde{C}$ are bounded above and below, Theorem~\ref{theorec} implies recurrence of both networks $(\Z^2,C)$ and $(\Z^2,\tilde{C})$.

nodes.name: $f_1=r/R$ and $f_2=R/r$ subharmonic
nodes.statement: By Proposition~\ref{propSubharmGen}, $f_1$ and $f_2$ are subharmonic on $\V$; reflecting through boundary lines extends them to $\Z^2$.

nodes.name: Maxima $M_1,M_2$ are bounded
nodes.statement: Using $\eqref{eqrngeneration}$ and $\eqref{eqrhosn}$, the product $M_1(n)M_2(n) \leq e^{8A}$, so the subharmonic $f_1,f_2$ are bounded.

nodes.name: Conclude $r\equiv R$
nodes.statement: Theorem~\ref{theosuperharm} gives that $M-f_1$ and $M-f_2$ are nonnegative superharmonic, hence constant on the recurrent network; so $f_1\equiv f_2\equiv 1$ and the patterns coincide.

nodes.name: Quasicrystallic rhombic embedding and circle pattern
nodes.section: 5.1 Quasicrystallic circle patterns and connection to $\Z^d$
nodes.statement: A rhombic embedding maps each face of $\mathscr{D}$ to a rhombus; if the number of distinct edge directions is $2d<\infty$, it is quasicrystallic with dimension $d$. Adding circles centered at white vertices with radius equal to edge length defines an isoradial quasicrystallic circle pattern.

nodes.name: Convention for `quasicrystallic'
nodes.section: 5.1 Quasicrystallic circle patterns and connection to $\Z^d$
nodes.statement: The notion `quasicrystallic' is not unique in the literature; here the definition of $\cite{BMS05}$ is adopted, only meaningful for infinite or growing graphs.

nodes.name: Monotonicity criterion for $\Omega_{\mathscr D}$
nodes.section: 5.1 Quasicrystallic circle patterns and connection to $\Z^d$
nodes.statement: Any two points of $\Omega_{\mathscr D}$ can be connected by a path with all directed edges lying in one $d$-dimensional octant of $\{\pm \mathbf{e}_1,\dots,\pm\mathbf{e}_d\}$.
assumptions: $\Omega_{\mathscr D}\subset \Z^d$ corresponds to a quasicrystallic rhombic embedding
conclusions: Any two points in $\Omega_{\mathscr D}$ are connected by a path with directed edges in a single $d$-dim octant

nodes.name: Quasicrystallic rhombic embedding from a plane
nodes.section: 5.1 Quasicrystallic circle patterns and connection to $\Z^d$
nodes.statement: From a 2-plane $E\subset\R^d$ and lattice $\mathcal{L}=c_1\Z\times\dots\times c_d\Z$, taking lattice points whose Voronoi cells meet $E$ produces an infinite monotone quad-surface $\Omega^{\mathcal L}(E)$ projecting to a rhombic embedding of the plane.

nodes.name: Boundary-preserving rebuilding (lem2patt)
nodes.section: 5.1 Quasicrystallic circle patterns and connection to $\Z^d$
nodes.statement: If $\mathscr{D},\mathscr{D}'$ are simply connected finite rhombic embeddings sharing edge directions and boundary faces, any (embedded) circle pattern $\mathscr{C}$ for $\mathscr{D}$ extends to an (embedded) circle pattern $\mathscr{C}'$ for $\mathscr{D}'$ agreeing on boundary circles.
assumptions: $\mathscr{D},\mathscr{D}'$ simply connected finite rhombic embeddings with the same edge directions
$\mathscr{C}$ is an embedded planar circle pattern for $\mathscr{D}$ and the labelling from the rhombic embedding
conclusions: There exists an embedded planar circle pattern $\mathscr{C}'$ for $\mathscr{D}'$ agreeing with $\mathscr{C}$ on boundary circles

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma lem2patt
nodes.section: 5.1 Quasicrystallic circle patterns and connection to $\Z^d$
nodes.statement: Extend the comparison function $w$ on the brick $\Pi$ (common to both quad-surfaces) using 3D-consistency of Hirota equation $\eqref{eqw}$; restrict to $\Omega_{\mathscr{D}'}$ to build $\mathscr{C}'$, with embeddedness following from boundary kite identification.

nodes.name: Embeddedness preserved under infinite flip
nodes.statement: If $\Omega'_{\mathscr{D}}$ results from $\Omega_{\mathscr{D}}$ by an infinite-strip flip and $\mathscr{C}$ is embedded, then the corresponding circle pattern $\mathscr{C}'$ for $\Omega'_{\mathscr{D}}$ is also embedded.
assumptions: $\Omega_{\mathscr D}'$ obtained from $\Omega_{\mathscr D}$ by a flip for a simply infinite strip
conclusions: The circle pattern $\mathscr{C}'$ corresponding to $\Omega_{\mathscr D}'$ is embedded

nodes.name: Rigidity of quasicrystallic isoradial circle patterns
nodes.section: 5.3 Uniqueness of isoradial quasicrystallic circle patterns
nodes.statement: For $\mathscr{D}\in\mathscr{E}$ and any embedded circle pattern $\mathscr{C}$ with the same combinatorics and intersection angles, $\mathscr{C}$ is the image of the isoradial circle pattern of $\mathscr{D}$ under a similarity of $\C$.
assumptions: $\mathscr{D}\in\mathscr{E}$ infinite quasicrystallic rhombic embedding (covers $\C$, brick contains a $\Z^2$-sublattice)
conclusions: $\mathscr{C}$ is the image of the isoradial circle pattern for $\mathscr{D}$ under a similarity of $\C$

nodes.name: Proof of rigidity of quasicrystallic isoradial circle patterns
nodes.section: 5.3 Uniqueness of isoradial quasicrystallic circle patterns
nodes.statement: Extend the comparison function $w$ to the brick $\Pi(\Omega_{\mathscr D})$; flips arrange arbitrary numbers of $\Z^2$-sublattice generations around any vertex, then Theorem~\ref{theoSGUniq} forces $w$ constant on each sublattice, hence everywhere.

nodes.name: Extend comparison function $w$ to brick
nodes.section: 5.3 Uniqueness of isoradial quasicrystallic circle patterns
nodes.statement: Define $w$ on $\Omega_{\mathscr D}$ by $\eqref{eqdefw}$ and uniquely extend it to $\Pi(\Omega_{\mathscr D})$ via the 3D-consistent Hirota equation $\eqref{eqw}$.

nodes.name: Use flips and $SG$ rigidity to fix $w$ on sublattices
nodes.section: 5.3 Uniqueness of isoradial quasicrystallic circle patterns
nodes.statement: Perform flips so a $\Z^2$-sublattice $\Omega(\hat{\mathbf z})$ has arbitrarily many generations; embeddedness is preserved (Lemma~\ref{lemEmbeddedInfFlip}) and Theorem~\ref{theoSGUniq} forces $w$ constant on white/black vertices of $\Omega(\hat{\mathbf z})$.

nodes.name: Conclude $w$ constant globally
nodes.section: 5.3 Uniqueness of isoradial quasicrystallic circle patterns
nodes.statement: The combinatorial assumption on $\mathscr{D}\in\mathscr{E}$ propagates the constancy of $w$ from sublattices to the whole brick, so $\mathscr{C}$ is isoradial up to similarity.

nodes.name: Combinatorial $K$-environment
nodes.section: 5.3 Uniqueness of isoradial quasicrystallic circle patterns
nodes.statement: The combinatorial $K$-environment of $z\in V(\mathscr{D})$ is the subgraph of all vertices with combinatorial distance at most $K$ from $z$ in $\mathscr{D}$.

nodes.name: Local convergence of radius ratio
nodes.section: 5.3 Uniqueness of isoradial quasicrystallic circle patterns
nodes.statement: For $\mathscr{D}\in\mathscr{E}$, $v_0$ a white vertex, there exist $n_0$ and $s_n(v_0,\mathscr{D})\to 0$ such that any embedded $\mathscr{C}_n$ on the $2n$-environment satisfies $|r_n(v_0)/r_n(v_1)-1|\leq s_n(v_0,\mathscr{D})$ for incident $v_1$.
conclusions: $\bigl|r_n(v_0)/r_n(v_1) - 1\bigr| \leq s_n(v_0,\mathscr{D})$ for all $v_1$ incident to $v_0$ in $G_n(v_0)$

nodes.name: Generalized Ring Lemma for quasicrystallic embeddings
nodes.section: 5.3 Uniqueness of isoradial quasicrystallic circle patterns
nodes.statement: For a quasicrystallic embedding $\mathscr{D}$ with $\alpha_{\min}=\min\alpha(e)$ and $n_0$ with $(n_0-3)\alpha_{\min}>\pi$: if $\mathscr{D}$ contains a $(2n_0)$-environment of a white vertex $v_0$, then $r(v_1)/r(v_0)>C(\mathscr{D})$ for any incident $v_1$.
assumptions: $r$ radius function of an embedded circle pattern
conclusions: There is $C(\mathscr{D})>0$ such that $r(v_1)/r(v_0)>C$ for all $v_1$ incident to $v_0$

nodes.name: Proof of generalized Ring Lemma (quasicrystallic)
nodes.section: 5.3 Uniqueness of isoradial quasicrystallic circle patterns
nodes.statement: Argue by contradiction: a sequence with $r_n(v_0)=1$ and $r_n(v_1)\to 0$ converges in $\hat{\C}$; iterating $\eqref{eqFgen}$ at most $n_0$ times forces overlapping kites in the limit, contradicting embeddedness.

nodes.name: Rodin-Sullivan-type rate for plane-based embeddings
nodes.section: 5.3 Uniqueness of isoradial quasicrystallic circle patterns
nodes.statement: For a plane-based quasicrystallic rhombic embedding, $s_n(v_0,\mathscr{D})\leq s_n(\mathscr{D})\leq C/n$ for $n\geq n_0(\mathscr{D})$ and any white $v_0$.
conclusions: $s_n(v_0,\mathscr{D}) \leq s_n(\mathscr{D}) \leq C/n$

nodes.name: Discrete map $Z^\gamma$ for general $\psi$
nodes.statement: For $0<\gamma<2$, $Z^\gamma:\Z_+^2\to\C$ solves $q(\dots)=e^{2i(\psi-\pi)}$ together with $\eqref{defZgamma2}$ and $Z^\gamma(0,0)=0$, $Z^\gamma(1,0)=1$, $Z^\gamma(0,1)=e^{\gamma(\pi-\psi)i}$.

nodes.name: Properties of $Z^\gamma$ at angle $\psi$
nodes.statement: (i) $(\gamma-1)(R(z)^2-R(z-i)R(z+1)-\cos\psi R(z)(R(z-i)-R(z+1)))\geq 0$ on $\V\setminus\{\pm N+iN\}$. (ii) $Z^\gamma$ is embedded for $0<\gamma<2$.
conclusions: Inequality $\eqref{eqRotDirectionpsi}$ holds on $\V\setminus\{\pm N+iN\mid N\in\N\}$
$Z^\gamma$ given by Definition $\ref{defZgammapsi}$ is embedded

nodes.name: Boundary values of $w$ on coordinate semi-axes
nodes.statement: $w(n e_k) = 1$ if $n=0$; $a_k^{\gamma-1}=e^{(\gamma-1)\log a_k}$ if $n$ odd; $\prod_{m=1}^{n/2}\frac{m-1+\gamma/2}{m-\gamma/2}$ if $n\geq 2$ even.

nodes.name: Embeddedness of quasicrystallic $Z^\gamma$-circle patterns
nodes.statement: Let $\Omega\subset\Z_+^d$ be a simply connected monotone quad-surface; the circle pattern given by $w$ with initial values $\eqref{eqdefsemi}$ is embedded.
conclusions: The circle pattern given by $w$ with initial values $\eqref{eqdefsemi}$ is embedded

nodes.name: Construction of quasicrystallic $Z^\gamma$ examples
nodes.statement: Veronika Schreiber's program builds the figures: rotational rhombic embeddings via 5- or 7-fold orthonormal bases and translations $t_1,t_2$, then $\gamma=5/p$ for integer $p\geq 3$ and Hirota propagation in $\Z^5$ or $\Z^7$.

nodes.name: Subharmonicity of radius ratio (general)
nodes.statement: Under convexity conditions $r_j\geq r_0\cos\alpha_j$ and $\rho_j\geq\rho_0\cos\alpha_j$, $\sum c_j r_j/\rho_j \geq \sum c_j r_0/\rho_0$ and similarly for $\rho/r$, with $c_j=\sin\alpha_j/((\rho_j/\rho_0)+(\rho_0/\rho_j)-2\cos\alpha_j)$.
assumptions: $\mathscr{D}$ quasicrystallic with labelling $\alpha$, two radius functions $r,\rho$
conclusions: $\sum_{j=1}^4 c_j (r_j/\rho_j) \geq \sum_{j=1}^4 c_j (r_0/\rho_0)$
$\sum_{j=1}^4 c_j (\rho_j/r_j) \geq \sum_{j=1}^4 c_j (\rho_0/r_0)$

nodes.name: Proof of subharmonicity (general)
nodes.statement: Taylor expand $f_\alpha(x+\log y)$ about $y=1$ using Lemma~\ref{lemPropf}(i); the convexity assumption $r_j\geq r_0\cos\alpha_j$ keeps the second-order term nonpositive, giving the inequality.

nodes.name: Convexity of $Z^\gamma$-kites
nodes.statement: If $\psi\geq\pi/2$ and $0<\gamma<2$, or $\psi<\pi/2$ with $(\pi-2\psi)/(\pi-\psi)\leq\gamma\leq\pi/(\pi-\psi)$, all kites in the $Z^\gamma$-circle pattern of Definition~\ref{defZgammapsi} are convex.
conclusions: All kites in the $Z^\gamma$-circle pattern of Definition $\ref{defZgammapsi}$ are convex

nodes.name: Proof of convexity of $Z^\gamma$-kites (Appendix)
nodes.statement: Combine Proposition~3 of $\cite{Agpsi}$ ($\eqref{eqZgammaR2psi}$) with Theorem~\ref{theoZgammapsi}; analyze rotation of the curves $\Gamma_n$ formed by $f_{n,m}$, treating $1<\gamma<2$ and using $\alpha\leq\psi$, $\pi/2-\psi\leq\beta\leq\pi/2$ to bound kite angles.

nodes.name: Rigidity of $Z^\gamma$-circle patterns at angle $\psi$
nodes.statement: Under the convexity-parameter range, the $Z^\gamma$-circle pattern is the unique embedded $SG$-pattern (up to scaling) for $\Z_+^2,\alpha_\psi$ covering the sector of angle $\gamma(\pi-\psi)$ with boundary centers on boundary half-lines and convex kites.
assumptions: Embedded $SG$-circle pattern for $\Z^2_+$ and $\alpha_\psi$ with sector $\beta\in[0,\gamma(\pi-\psi)]$
Boundary circle centers on the boundary half-lines
All kites at intersecting circles convex
conclusions: The pattern equals the $Z^\gamma$-circle pattern of Def. $\ref{defZgammapsi}$ up to global scaling

nodes.name: Rigidity of $Z^\gamma$-circle patterns on a cone
nodes.statement: Gluing four $Z^\gamma$-patterns on $\Z_\pm\times\Z_\pm$ yields a circle pattern $\mathscr{C}_\gamma$ on a cone of cone angle $2\pi\gamma$; any embedded pattern with the same combinatorics, intersection angles, an apex circle, and convex kites coincides with $\mathscr{C}_\gamma$ (up to scaling and rotation).
assumptions: Embedded circle pattern with same combinatorics/intersection angles, one circle center at the cone apex, only convex kites
conclusions: The pattern coincides with $\mathscr{C}_\gamma$ up to scaling and rotation about the apex

nodes.name: Rigidity of quasicrystallic $Z^\gamma$-circle patterns I
nodes.statement: For $\mathscr{D}$ quasicrystallic covering $\C$ with $\Pi(\Omega_{\mathscr{D}})=\Z^d$ and $\gamma\in[(\pi-2\psi_{\min})/(\pi-\psi_{\min}),\pi/(\pi-\psi_{\min})]$, any embedded pattern with the same combinatorics, intersection angles, apex circle, and per-sublattice convex kites equals $\mathscr{C}_\gamma$ up to scaling/rotation.
assumptions: $\mathscr{D}$ quasicrystallic rhombic embedding covering $\C$, with edge directions $\mathcal A$ in general position
Embedded circle pattern $\mathscr{C}$ with apex circle, convex kites on each $\Z^2$-sublattice with two coord axes
conclusions: $\mathscr{C}$ coincides with $\mathscr{C}_\gamma$ up to scaling and rotation about the apex of the cone

nodes.name: Rigidity of quasicrystallic $Z^\gamma$-circle patterns II
nodes.statement: If all intersection angles of $\alpha$ exceed $\pi/2$ and the origin is white, then any embedded circle pattern with the same combinatorics covering the same cone with apex-centered origin circle and convex kites equals $\mathscr{C}_\gamma$ up to scaling/rotation.
assumptions: $\mathscr{C}$ embedded circle pattern for $(\mathscr{D},\alpha)$ covering the same cone, origin circle at apex, all kites convex
conclusions: $\mathscr{C}$ coincides with $\mathscr{C}_\gamma$ up to scaling and rotation about the apex

nodes.name: Recurrence of simple random walk on $G$
nodes.statement: For a quasicrystallic rhombic embedding $\mathscr{D}$ covering $\C$ with associated white-vertex graph $G$, the simple random walk on $G$ is recurrent.
assumptions: $G$ infinite associated graph built from white vertices
conclusions: The simple random walk on $G$ is recurrent

nodes.name: Proof of recurrence on quasicrystallic $G$
nodes.statement: Bound rhombi areas below by $C_1$, partition $G$ into annular shells $V_k$ with $\varrho_k=4k$, shorten each $V_k$ to a single vertex; the shortened network has $R_{\text{eff}}'=\sum 1/|E_k|=\infty$, so $G$ is recurrent.
